MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 13, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on February 13, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 8, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation; Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case).

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  February 13, 2018
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received information on one Closed Session
matter regarding potential initiation of litigation. The City Council provided direction to staff but
no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the City on Receiving the "Government Finance Officers Association’s
  Distinguished Budget Presentation Award"

  Mayor Sachs presented the award to Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction that his recent request for public records was denied
due to attorney-client privilege.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that the City and the Nadadores should hire a marketing firm for public
outreach regarding the opportunity for naming rights at the Marguerite Aquatics Center.

Mark Speros, M.V.: speaking as President of the Highland Park Homeowners Association Board
of Directors, he stated that members of his community were surprised to learn that very major
decisions were made during the holidays regarding Verizon Wireless’ installation of additional
structures on a tower near their neighborhood.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the City's process for consideration of voting districting has been
so bad that she cannot even call it a dog and pony show.

Dale Rathburn, M.V.: announced that he emailed all of the Council Members and has been
speaking with staff regarding the residential drug rehab facility next door to his home. He asked
when he can expect a response to his email.

Steven LaMotte, M.V.: speaking as a Board Member for the South Orange County Economic
Coalition, he thanked the City for its support and invited the Council Members to the 2018
Economic Preview event on February 23 from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at the Outlets in San
Clemente.

Michael Ashley, M.V.: on behalf of the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce, he invited the
community to participate in or volunteer for the Oso Fit 5K run on Saturday March 3, 2018. Mr.
Ashley said that more than 100 people have signed up and 100% of pre-registration fees go to the
charity or non-profit of the participant's choice.

City Council Minutes  2  February 13, 2018
 Ryan Reza Farsai, M.V.: announced that he has sold his business interests to his brothers and is
moving out of state. He said he officially responded to a letter from the City Attorney and he held
a yoga class at the corner of La Paz and Marguerite to demonstrate his ownership rights to that
property.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 23, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated January 12, 2018 in the Amount of $925,298.24

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated January 19, 2018 in the Amount of $1,741,957.16

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 26, 2018 in the Amount of $2,183,303.19

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Felipe Tennis Center Name Change

  Approved the recommended name change from "Felipe Tennis Center" to "Felipe Tennis
  & Recreation Center."

6.  Los Alisos Boulevard and Santa Margarita Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP
  238)

  Authorized issuance of a purchase order to civTEC Consulting in an amount not to exceed
  $50,000 for design engineering services for the subject project.

7.  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 18837)

City Council Minutes  3  February 13, 2018
   Authorized issuance of a purchase order to GMU Geotechnical, Inc. for materials testing
  services in an amount to exceed $48,875.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2017

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  December 2017

  Received and filed.

11.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2017

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

12.  Fifth Public Hearing Regarding District Election Consideration: California Voting
  Rights of 2001 Allegation; City Response to Racially Polarized Voting; Consideration
  and Action Upon Alternative Remedial Actions

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Mayor Sachs opened the public hearing at 7:04 p.m.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: asked if the City's demographic expert can use statistical analysis to
  determine how he voted in city elections.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she has changed her position and now agrees with the
  transition to districts. She expressed support for any of the maps except Map Z and asked
  how often the districts would be updated.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: said that Mission Viejo is at a point where it must change its election
  system and she expressed dissatisfaction with the way the City handled the process.

  Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: stated that she does not agree with district voting and the City
  Council needs to consider other alternatives. She expressed her appreciation for the City's
  efforts in this process.
City Council Minutes  4  February 13, 2018
   Jessica Riegert, M.V.: said that factors such as poverty and lack of healthcare should be
  considered when looking at districts. She noted that she is against maps A and L and she
  feels that Map G best fulfills the requirements.

  Judith Fike, M.V.: stated that she is in favor of district based elections simply because it is
  more democratic and there is more accountability. She said she would be better served as
  a resident if she had one Council Member to tend to her area and she prefers Map G.

  Nancy Sandoval, M.V.: declared that districts would only polarize the City more. She said
  she supports at-large elections and wants to be able to vote for all candidates.

  Mayor Sachs closed the public hearing at 7:31 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  direct the City Attorney and staff to look for appropriate remedies for Polarized Voting,
  tailored to the facts presented in the City of Mission Viejo, and return to the City Council
  with information and recommendations at the next Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

13.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies and Salary Schedule

  Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 18-09 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies; and (2)
  adopt Resolution 18-10 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule Effective February 13, 2018.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs presented the report.

City Council Minutes  5  February 13, 2018
 15.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Chief Capobianco presented the report.

17.  Library and Cultural Services Update

  Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum discussed her attendance at the opening day for Mission Viejo Girls
Softball which, she said, was a fun and colorful event. She complimented the City’s new police
chief, Lieutenant “Q” Vuong, on his communication skills both with the City Council and with the
public. She said that Q’s use of social media is phenomenal and the way he’s working with his
staff to connect with residents is great. She has noticed a lot more police presence on the streets
and residents have reported seeing officers on bikes on the trails and near the lake. Council
Member Bucknum discussed a fundraiser called Purse Palooza that will benefit the Friends of the
Mission Viejo Library. Residents can donate gently used purses in collection bins at the recreation
centers or at businesses such as Kwik Copy Printing and High Park Tap House. The purses will be
sold on May 5 in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Council Member Bucknum said she has
attended public hearings and Coastal Commission hearings for a long time as an advocate for the
completion of an alternative to the 5 freeway. She noted that it would have to be in the form of a
Transportation Corridor Agency toll road as that is the only agency that has managed to build a
new road in Orange County. She stated that San Clemente’s attack on stopping the toll road is a
direct attack on the City of Mission Viejo and the beltway that San Clemente proposed goes
directly through Mission Viejo. Council Member Bucknum said that San Clemente’s theme has
been to let other people take care of traffic problems but it is very important to understand that the
completion of a north south route is vital for South County residents, for commerce and for
emergency services. She also observed that development continues everywhere and cities must
realize that traffic is a regional issue and they must work together for a solution. In closing, Council
Member Bucknum applauded Mayor Sachs for representing the region on the Toll Road agency
and for being fair in looking at all alternatives, even when it could be detrimental to his own city.

City Council Minutes  6  February 13, 2018
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell addressed some comments that were made during the public hearing
earlier. He apologized to Mrs. Fike for not replying to the email that she mentioned. He said he
tries to respond to everything but he receives 20 to 50 emails a day from people in San Clemente
who attack the Council about the toll road. That is in addition to all of the other business emails
and he said it can be a bit overwhelming at times. He noted that for the most part, the Council
Members do a good job of responding and getting involved when they can. For example, he said
he is working with resident Michael Rotcher to look at Community Choice energy as a possibility
for the residents of Mission Viejo. Council Member Goodell also addressed Mr. Gilbert’s
accusation that the Brown Act has been violated by this City Council as a matter of course. He
said that he hasn’t found that to be true but rather, the Council has been very, very careful and is
aware of the limitations of the Brown Act. The Council Members hold the line on that so, he said,
he wanted to respond to the accusation to make residents aware that the City Council will continue
to maintain integrity, follow the law and represent all residents in an open and transparent way.
Council Member Goodell outlined his attendance at a meeting with the South Orange County
Watershed Management group as well as a presentation on the statewide water project that will
replace the aging system that brings water from Northern California south. He said important
decisions are being made and the City Council is working hard to stay in front of issues and
represent the residents of Mission Viejo the best they can.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed the volunteer planting day at Marguerite Aquatics Center and
noted that she was overwhelmed by the turnout of Nadadores swimmers and divers and their
families. She said it is volunteer efforts like these that save the City a considerable amount of
money and it is a great exercise in community. She also toured the Aquatics Center that day and
received an update on the progress. She said that the facility is beautiful and will be another jewel
in the crown of Mission Viejo and she has been impressed with the resourcefulness of the City
Council and staff who have been careful to be very cost efficient with the project. Council Member
Kelley announced that on February 9 she attended a discussion on homelessness in Orange County
led by 5th District Supervisor Lisa Bartlett. She learned what is being done and what can be done
on the issue and she said there needs to be a lot of education and collaboration and cities should
take a regional approach to the problem. Council Member Kelley also discussed her attendance at
the Mission Viejo Girls Softball opening day and said it was wonderful to see the league playing
on the beautiful William Craycraft Park fields. In closing, Council Member Kelley announced that
the Community of Character word for the month of February is unity and the movie to depict that
quality is Local Hero. The screening is free and will be shown on Sunday, February 18, 2018 at
2:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths challenged Mayor Sachs to participate with him in the Oso Fit 5k Fun Run
and said he's looking forward to it. He also thanked Lt. “Q” Vuong for all that he is doing to get
the Sheriff’s Department officers out in the community more.

City Council Minutes  7  February 13, 2018
 Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs stated that he was really excited to learn that Chief “Q” is getting out in the
community more and there is a lot of policing going on. He said there are officers on bicycles out
on the trails and they are doing a great job of getting into the local business areas as well. Mayor
Sachs reemphasized what Council Member Goodell said about Brown Act and noted that he's been
on the losing side of two votes because of the Brown Act. He isn’t able to talk to his colleagues to
try and persuade them to his thinking and therefore the Council does its deliberating on the dais.
Mayor Sachs noted that one of his goals for the year is to implement an expedited "Building Permit
in a Day Program." He said that very soon, residents will be able to schedule an appointment, on
a first-come, first-served basis by calling 949-470-3054. Six appointments will be held every
Wednesday for qualified projects to be reviewed and potentially completed in the same day. Some
of the projects that qualify are residential remodels, one story additions, decks, patio covers,
swimming pools and spas, residential retaining walls, and tenant improvements at The Shops at
Mission Viejo. Mayor Sachs said this program is business and community friendly and he
encouraged residents to take advantage of it.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:15 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 27, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

_____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 27, 2018

City Council Minutes  8  February 13, 2018
